A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPGM/OPGM-rs research despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A-B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original OPGM/OPGM-rs benchmark results, matching-bias ablations, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements in Section 8 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a failure-mode analysis across four visual matching datasets in Appendix B, Figure 3.

M1.justification: Sections 4-7 retain the weighted-TV objective, linear-assignment reduction and mapping, affinity and matching-bias components, and partial matching loss. The revised introduction explains the existing reduction without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate SPair-71K, Pascal VOC Keypoint, IMCPT 50/100, and yeast PPI matching with 5-25% added-edge noise. The new failure analysis reuses the four existing visual datasets without introducing another task or test environment.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain the same NGM-v2 and GCAN comparator configurations, including AFAT-U and AFAT-I. The runtime comparison retains GCAN, AFAT-I, and AFAT-U, while Table 4 retains SIGMA and StableGM. Newly discussed related methods are not added to these evaluations.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a diagnostic evaluation measuring partiality error, mismatching error, and their sum as percentages of ground-truth matches. Previously stated benchmark metrics, training settings, noise levels, and the 3,000-pair runtime evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds a failure-mode analysis separating true matches rejected by the feasibility threshold from feasible true matches that are nevertheless missed, with evidence across four datasets in Figure 3. Existing matching-bias ablations, parameter sensitivity, noise robustness, and efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 8.1 retains five random starts and 95% confidence intervals for image-keypoint results. Existing uncertainty reporting is unchanged, and Figure 3 introduces no additional run counts, intervals, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1-4 and Figure 2 are unchanged; OPGM-rs mean F1 remains 57.8 ± 0.2 on SPair-71K and 72.7 ± 0.2 on IMCPT 100. Figure 3 adds error rates showing partiality error exceeding mismatching error on all four visual datasets.

T1.justification: The optimization definitions, theorems, and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged. Appendix B adds quantitative definitions of partiality and mismatching error using the existing feasibility condition, with total error defined as their sum. This is a limited definitional addition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a weighted-TV partial-matching objective, exact solutions through linear assignment with cubic worst-case complexity, and an end-to-end architecture with partial matching loss. The revised embedding explanation does not extend these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains how low learned affinity and consequently high matching cost can make ground-truth pairs infeasible. This provides a specific false-negative mechanism beyond the retained discussion of ambiguous annotations and noisy inputs.

D1.justification: The implementation information remains the same, including the SciPy assignment solver, ThinkMatch access link, hardware, Adam schedules, and hyperparameter grids. The new failure analysis supplies no additional implementation or access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 substantially expands positioning through comparisons with transport-based graph matching, partial-transport subgraph matching, spectral approaches, and universe-based partial matching. It distinguishes matching constraints and class-specific assumptions, adds works including Pan et al. (2024) and Nurlanov et al. (2023), and removes the LinSATNet discussion and citation.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Optimal Partial Graph Matching' to 'Learning Partial Graph Matching via Optimal Partial Transport,' and one author affiliation changes. Related-work passages are rewritten, the introduction clarifies the assignment embedding, and sensitivity/runtime prose is condensed; the overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the grouped-bar failure-analysis Figure 3 in Appendix B. Existing Figures 1-2 and Tables 1-4 retain their displays, with limited placement and page-flow changes, including Figure 2 moving lower on page 9.

improvement.justification: The expanded Section 2.1 clarifies distinctions from adjacent research, while Appendix B adds useful quantitative insight into missed matches. These improve positioning and diagnostic understanding. The gains are limited: central methods, proofs, and benchmark results remain unchanged, and Figure 3 does not identify the evaluated model variant or report uncertainty.
